_comment: Field NAMES both runtimes' flight recorders must agree on. Read by typescript/src/flight-recorder/key-redaction-parity.test.ts and python/tests/test_key_redaction_parity.py, so a name added to one runtime's list cannot silently miss the other. Its sibling value-redaction-corpus.json covers the other half of the question: that file asks whether a VALUE looks like a secret, this one asks whether a KEY says it is one. A value that looks like nothing in particular -- an opaque random string, which is what most API keys and session keys are -- can only be caught by its key.
_must_redact_comment: Every name here was written to the flight log in the clear before this corpus existed, in both runtimes. The rules matched `token`, `secret` and `authorization` as exact words while matching `password`, `credential` and `cookie` as prefixes, so the singular of the first three was redacted and the plural was not. The qualified `*Key` names were missed by a different gap: a fixed substring list held `apikey` and `privatekey` but not `sshKey`, `signingKey` or the rest.
_must_keep_comment: Redacting these would be a bug of the opposite kind, and the flight recorder is deliberately conservative about it: a ledger that redacts too much keeps the record and loses the ability to read it. `key`, `auth`, `salt`, `nonce`, `bearer`, `id`, `name` and `path` are left readable on purpose -- `key` alone is one of the most common field names there is (map entries, config entries, sort keys, and the keyboard shortcut Show-and-Tell records), and `bearer` appears in this codebase only as a local variable, never as a recorded field. Values that actually look like credentials are still caught by value-redaction-corpus.json regardless of the name they arrive under.
_counts_comment: `token` is the one secret word that is also a unit of measurement. Usage accounting records these on every provider call, and a bare number cannot be a credential, so the VALUE decides: these names are redacted when they carry a string and kept when they carry a number. The name alone cannot tell `apiTokens` from `inputTokens`.
